problem.text: The shared parser hardcoded an 8192-token cache default, while eval/longctx.py already requested default_cache_size=65536 through an unsupported keyword.

reasoning.text: Adding an optional default_cache_size parameter lets applications choose their default without changing the existing command-line option. The same value supplies both argparse's default and its help text.

impact.text: The change removes the long-context entry point's unsupported-keyword failure. Callers omitting the new parameter retain 8192; cache=False still omits cache arguments.

source_notes.text: The parent annotation identified the long-context script's argument-registration failure; inspection of this diff shows that specific incompatibility is removed, not carried over.

PR #22, “OpenAI compatible API example,” discusses an API example and cache_quant usage. Its relationship here is only inferred from its use of model_init.add_args and cache options; it does not establish motivation for this default-cache change.

limitations: Validation executed an isolated parent helper and a reconstruction incorporating the inspected diff, not the complete package or evaluation script. Model loading, GPU allocation and long-context inference were not tested.

claims.text: default_cache_size is a Python helper argument, not a new CLI flag. The existing -cs/--cache_size remains an integer option. Its default remains 8192 tokens unless the application supplies another value.

The parsed cache_size flows unchanged through model_init.init into Cache(max_num_tokens=...) for both FP16 and quantized cache construction. Thus 65536 in longctx.py requests token capacity, rather than changing cache precision or a generation-length limit.

An isolated argparse check reproduced the parent's unexpected-keyword TypeError. With the inspected changes applied to the extracted helper, omitted overrides yielded 8192, an application override yielded 65536, explicit -cs 4096 took precedence, and cache=False produced no cache fields. The overridden help text also passed its check.

annotation.summary: Adds application-specific cache defaults while preserving the 8192-token fallback and explicit CLI overrides, resolving longctx.py's unsupported keyword.
